title: What If Every Cloud on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every cloud vanished tonight? You'd expect sunny skies. The real shock is the heat.
Clouds cover about 70 percent of Earth at any moment, and they act like a giant white sunshade.
They reflect sunlight back to space. Satellites show the net effect of clouds on climate is cooling.
Take them away and one university estimate says average surface temperatures could rise by as much as 22 degrees Celsius.
Rain would not stop entirely, but the water cycle would be wrecked, and most habitats would not survive that jump.
The sky you complain about on gray days is quietly holding the climate together.
